# AI vs RS - Testing a system generated by Github Copilot
This project aims to test a simple booking system for DnD, generated by Github co-pilot. 
The goal is to show that I can provide comprehensive testing of a system; including defining requirements, test cases, and provide comprehensive automated testing. 

## Important for employers 
If you are looking for a minimal system test using the same stack as the main project, see [The subsystem paragraph](#subsystem)

## Preliminaries 
To provide addtional transparency and increase my learning, I have set the following rules: 
- Github Copilot shall not write any test, testcase, or requirement. 
- I shall provide a comprehensive list of the resources used to complete this project
- I shall explicitly state which testing strategies are used

## Resources
These are the articles, papers, and technical reports that I have to use in this project.
- [Harvard guide on prompting](https://www.huit.harvard.edu/news/ai-prompts)
- [IEEE guide to requirement specification](https://www.computer.org/resources/software-requirements-specifications?source=resources)software-requirements-specifications#requirements-fundamentals
- [Testability review paper1](https://dl.acm.org/doi/epdf/10.1145/2851613.2851978)
- [Formal testability paper](https://hal.science/hal-00852373v1/document)
- [EARS model of creating formal requirements](https://www.iaria.org/conferences2013/filesICCGI13/ICCGI_2013_Tutorial_Terzakis.pdf)

## Subsystem
This project contains a minimal system test in the subsystem_example folder.

The purpose for this inclusion, is to showcase the features of the main project succiently in an systematic manner, as well as provide me with a place to experiment with testing strategy.
